summary: Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Uppsala University as assistant, deputy, and full professor (1927).
Jaroslav Průšek was a sinologist who studied at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts from circa 1924 to 1928. He also taught Karel Werner.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied under Peter Oldmeadow at the University of Sydney and earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford, SOAS as a postdoctoral fellow, and the University of Alberta.
Jason M. Wirth works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki and became professor of philosophy at Seattle University circa 2007.

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and completed his PhD under Gregory Schopen at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he also served as a lecturer.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin and earned his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon, later serving at Wilfrid Laurier University.

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held appointments as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica and visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Naropa University, the University of Delaware under Alan Fox, and the University of Virginia, where he completed his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard. He served as assistant professor at UC Berkeley, full professor at Cornell (1981–1985), and Diebold Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Philology at Harvard from 1998.

Jay L. Garfield is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under numerous Tibetan teachers. His career includes professorships at Hampshire College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Smith College, the University of Melbourne, and NUS.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni works in Indology and philosophy. He earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, later holding posts at Banaras Hindu University, McMaster, the University of Marburg (1991–2012), and the University of Innsbruck (circa 2012–2017).
Jayashree D. Sathe is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who served as editor in chief and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Jaś Elsner works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge (BA, PhD), Harvard, and the Courtauld Institute, later holding posts at the Courtauld, Corpus Christi College, and the University of Oxford as professor from 2014.
Jean Dantinne was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He taught at the Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966), and held research posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He served at EPHE, held a chair at Collège de France (1951–1978), and directed both the EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Liège and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Liège, and Collège de France (1993).
Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist who studied at the École Polytechnique from circa 1964 to 1966 and later served as its director from circa 1992 to 1999.

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck at the University of Amsterdam. He served with the Archaeological Survey of India and directed Leiden University and the Kern Institute.
